theorem.exactDescent: For a surjective linear map P:X->Y and F:X->X, a unique f:Y->Y with PF=fP exists iff ker(P) is F-invariant.
theorem.certificateFactorization: A certificate D factors through P iff D is constant on every fibre of P.
theorem.detectorIntersection: For a stacked linear detector D=(D1,D2), ker(D)=ker(D1) intersect ker(D2); common apparatus symmetries remain invisible to every invariant component.
theorem.composition: For X--P1->Y--P2->Z with defects Delta1=P1F-f1P1 and Delta2=P2f1-f2P2, Delta21=(P2P1)F-f2(P2P1)=P2Delta1+Delta2P1.
theorem.hiddenStateElimination: For F=[[A,B],[C,D]], exact elimination gives y_(n+1)=A y_n+B D^n h_0+sum_(j=0)^(n-1) B D^(n-1-j) C y_j. Kernel invariance is B=0; otherwise the exact shadow carries memory and initial slip.

approximate.errorBound: ||Delta x||_2 <= ||Delta||_2 ||x||_2; here the only leak is 0.02 times the hidden coordinate.

memoryClosureWitness.conclusion: Non-invariant hidden directions admit exact non-Markovian visible closure even when autonomous Markovian descent is impossible.

commutatorNoGo.statement: If PA=RP and PB=HP for a surjective P and commuting A,B, then [R,H]P=P[A,B]=0, hence [R,H]=0. A noncommuting target pair therefore cannot be the exact image of a commuting source pair.

nonlinearDetectorWitness.conclusion: A nonlinear certificate can split a selected linear-detector fibre, but this two-state witness is not a tomography theorem.

az052.conclusion: Bound count alone is not a sufficient certificate for the phase or boundary-response shadow.
